_readme: Year Slider config for the Greater Male' road simulator. Every value carries a status so nothing estimated is shown as official. Edit freely; app.js reads this file at start-up.

baseline.note: IUM report active-fleet figure; data collected in 2024 (confirmed by project owner). Type mix = Table 3 as coded in app.js.

fleet_index_vs_2024._note: Fleet of a vehicle group in a year divided by the same group in 2024. 2024 = 1 by construction. One series per vehicle type (data/years.json v2).

pickup.source: NBS Table 11.3 national registered 'Pick-Up' 2021-2023 (3,377 / 3,572 / 3,851) gives the 2021-2023 shape. 2023->2024 growth assumed 1.0679 (geometric mean of 2021-23 growth, limited to 0.97-1.25); 2025 and 2026 growth damped x0.75 per year. 2024 = 1 by construction. No published source beyond 2023.

other.source: Residual group (NBS total minus every mapped row: 3,299 / 3,716 / 4,187), mostly construction/industrial plant, tricycles and other. Same extrapolation rule (growth 1.1266); 2025-2026 are assumptions.

moto.source: Owner-supplied multipliers vs 2021 (1.00,1.10,1.23,1.31,1.39,1.40) divided by the 2024 value. 2022 and 2023 agree with NBS Table 11.3 (1.107 and 1.224 vs 2021). 2024-2026 are not in the published NBS table (ends 2023) and are unverified.

car.source: 2021-2023 shape from NBS Table 11.3 cars (8,606 / 9,998 / 12,044). Level anchored by assuming 2023->2024 growth of 1.147 (owner-supplied 1.33/1.16). 2025-2026 growth from owner-supplied 1.50 and 1.56 vs 2021. The owner's 2021-2022 car multipliers (1.00, 0.97) conflict with NBS (+16%) and were not used.

accidents.share_note: Owner assumption: 80% of Maldives Police Service accident counts are in Greater Male'. Not verified against the police data.

series.note: 2,379 recorded up to mid-October 2026 scaled by 365/288. Seasonality ignored.

accidents.source: Maldives Police Service counts as compiled by MV+ (supplied by owner). Not the 16,242 five-year figure, which could not be reconciled with this series.

model.caveat: beta is a modelling choice, not a measured causal elasticity. Reporting changes, post-COVID recovery and growth in Hulhumale also raise recorded accidents.

nbs_table_11_3_national_registered.note: National, cumulative registrations (not active, not Greater Male' only). Table ends 2023.

type_group_note: Each of the 18 types has its own series. scooter and escoot both use NBS 'Battery Scooter'; 'other' is the residual of the NBS total. Motorcycle and car series are unchanged from v1.

nbs_table_11_3_by_type.note: National cumulative registrations by type, used only for the 2021-2023 shape of each type. Sim counts come from the IUM report Table 3, not from NBS.

usage._readme: Time-of-day module. Moving share of type t at hour h = peak_share[t] x curve(h). Parked share = 1 - moving share. The same shares apply in every year (the report gives none per year).
usage.source: IUM report Table 30 (use of vehicles, hourly) and Table 31 (peak hours).

peak_share.default_note: 13,159 vehicles per hour / 119,093 fleet (Table 30 total / Table 3 total).
peak_share.by_type_note: Table 30 hourly count / Table 3 count for the types Table 30 lists. Other types use the default. Scooter is left at the default because Table 30's battery-scooter row (daily 210) does not match the 1,473 fleet.

report_figures.note: Weekly = 7 x daily, so every day of the week is given the same daily volume; only the shape differs. For most types hourly = daily / 6.

weekday.label: Sun-Thu
weekday.curve_status: assumption: peaks at the report's windows, with 1.0 = the observed peak hour; the rest is interpolated.

friday.label: Friday
friday.peaks_source: Table 31, weekends (10:00-10:30, 13:00-14:00) and note: Friday evening peak 16:00-21:00.
friday.curve_status: assumption; scaled so the day has the same total volume as a weekday.

saturday.label: Saturday
saturday.peaks_source: Table 31, weekends (10:00-10:30, 13:00-14:00) and note: Saturday evening peak 16:00-20:00.
saturday.curve_status: assumption; scaled so the day has the same total volume as a weekday.

usage.week_note: Days are numbered 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday. Sun-Thu are treated as weekdays and Fri/Sat as the weekend; the report says only 'weekdays' and 'weekends'.
